classification.difficultyReason: Choose a linear rearrangement, substitute into the nonlinear equation, simplify and factorise, then pair each root with its corresponding second coordinate.

answer.worked:
From the first equation, $y=15-x$. Substituting:
$$\begin{align*}x^2+(15-x)^2&=125\\2x^2-30x+100&=0\\x^2-15x+50&=0\\(x-5)(x-10)&=0\\x&=5\text{ or }10\end{align*}$$
From $y=15-x$, the corresponding values are $y=10$ or $5$. Hence $(x,y)=(5,10)$ or $(10,5)$.

From the first equation, $y=x-3$. Substituting:
$$\begin{align*}x^2+(x-3)^2&=185\\2x^2-6x-176&=0\\x^2-3x-88&=0\\(x-11)(x+8)&=0\\x&=11\text{ or }-8\end{align*}$$
From $y=x-3$, the corresponding values are $y=8$ or $-11$. Hence $(x,y)=(11,8)$ or $(-8,-11)$.

From the first equation, $y=5-2x$. Substituting:
$$\begin{align*}4x^2+(5-2x)^2&=17\\8x^2-20x+8&=0\\2x^2-5x+2&=0\\(2x-1)(x-2)&=0\\x&=\frac12\text{ or }2\end{align*}$$
From $y=5-2x$, the corresponding values are $y=4$ or $1$. Hence $(x,y)=(\frac12,4)$ or $(2,1)$.

From the first equation, $y=9-x$. Substituting:
$$\begin{align*}x^2+x(9-x)+(9-x)^2&=61\\x^2-9x+81&=61\\x^2-9x+20&=0\\(x-4)(x-5)&=0\\x&=4\text{ or }5\end{align*}$$
From $y=9-x$, the corresponding values are $y=5$ or $4$. Hence $(x,y)=(4,5)$ or $(5,4)$.

From the first equation, $y=\frac{5-x}{2}$. Substituting:
$$\begin{align*}2x\left(\frac{5-x}{2}\right)-x^2&=3\\5x-2x^2&=3\\2x^2-5x+3&=0\\(2x-3)(x-1)&=0\\x&=\frac32\text{ or }1\end{align*}$$
From $y=\frac{5-x}{2}$, the corresponding values are $y=\frac74$ or $2$. Hence $(x,y)=(\frac32,\frac74)$ or $(1,2)$.

From the first equation, $y=\frac{16-3x}{2}$. Substituting:
$$\begin{align*}x\left(\frac{16-3x}{2}\right)&=10\\16x-3x^2&=20\\3x^2-16x+20&=0\\(3x-10)(x-2)&=0\\x&=\frac{10}{3}\text{ or }2\end{align*}$$
From $y=\frac{16-3x}{2}$, the corresponding values are $y=3$ or $5$. Hence $(x,y)=(\frac{10}{3},3)$ or $(2,5)$.
